segmentation.text: The fact that the speed of a vehicle is lower than the prescribed limits
does not relieve
a driver
from the duty to decrease speed
when approaching and crossing an intersection,
when approaching and going around a curve,
when approaching a hill crest,
when traveling upon any narrow or winding highway,
or when special hazards exist or may exist
with respect to pedestrians or other traffic,
or by reason of weather
or other highway conditions,
and speed must be decreased
as may be necessary to avoid colliding
with any person, vehicle or other conveyance
on or entering a highway
in compliance with legal requirements and the duty of all persons to use due care.

elements.justification: The words keep the duty in force on the subject's speed: kin.speed is the 'magnitude of velocity' in m/s; the duty that is not relieved is a duty on that magnitude. Its 'Not a stand-in for' clauses do not concern speed itself.

'a driver' is, by DEF-NRS-484A-080, 'every person who drives or is in actual physical control of a vehicle': the duty binds the vehicle the driver controls. 'vehicle' is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle ('every device in, upon or by which any person or property is or may be transported or drawn upon a highway'); ru.aggregate is 'membership of a legal aggregate', and it is not used for the relational role of driving, which is read through the vehicle's controlled motion (observable_reading agency).

Reuses the index mapping of 'approaching an intersection' (NRS_484B_250_1). Approaching: the subject occupies (rel.occupies, 'a road user's footprint overlaps a lane / region') a travel region (st.travel_region) whose entrance end is an intersection (st.lane_enters, 'the intersection region a directed approach carrier runs into at its entrance end'); crossing: the subject occupies the intersection itself (st.intersection, 'the region where two roadways meet'). The occupancy is not a stand-in for geometry; lane_enters is not read from distance or velocity, as its contract requires.

A curve is the roadway's horizontal bend: st.curvature, 'horizontal curvature of the roadway at a point, as a magnitude (1/m, never negative)', read at the subject's place on the roadway it occupies (rel.occupies, st.roadway), standing clear of zero by the map's resolution p.curvature_resolution (a feature named without a measure is its presence). Going around it: that holds at the observation; approaching it: it holds at some observation of the window ahead whose length is p.curve_approach_reach of distance the subject travels (a .path window, which reads kin.path_length, 'distance travelled along the body's path'). Not kin.yaw_rate, which the ontology says is 'Not a stand-in for: road curvature'.

Reuses the index mapping of 'When approaching the crest of a grade' (NRS_484B_213_2a). st.crest is 'the place on a roadway's longitudinal profile where the slope changes from rising to falling in the direction of travel, carried as a region with a reference point and a boundary, so the ground distance from a road user to it is read through st.region_geometry'; approaching is the crest's reference point lying ahead of the subject's velocity (kin.position, kin.velocity) with the ground distance within p.crest_near_reach. st.crest is not the slope at a point (st.grade) nor the sight distance, which are not used for the place.

Traveling upon a highway: the subject occupies a lane (rel.occupies, st.lane, 'a longitudinal strip of roadway for one line of vehicles') lying on a highway (st.on_way, 'the public way a structure region lies on'; st.highway, 'the entire public way between its boundary lines'). Narrow: st.lane_width, 'width of a lane at a point', of that lane at or below p.narrow_lane_width. Winding: st.curvature of the roadway at the subject's place clear of p.curvature_resolution.

'pedestrians' is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-165::pedestrian ('a person afoot, a person in a manual or motorized wheelchair, or a person on an electric personal assistive mobility device'); 'other traffic' is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-285::traffic ('pedestrians, ridden or herded animals, vehicles and other conveyances ... using any highway for purposes of travel'). A hazard with respect to them is read through a pedestrian occupying a roadway (rel.occupies, st.roadway, 'the part of a highway improved for vehicular traffic') or a traffic road user whose centre approaches the subject's (prim.closest_approach_within, prim.closest_approach_distance). The primitives are 'Not a stand-in for: contact between bodies ... or the danger of a crash' alone: the danger is the operationalization of s9 that bounds them.

Weather is read through env.precipitation ('rain or snow falling'), env.wet_road ('road surface wet, standing water'), env.ice_or_snow ('road surface icy or snow-covered') and env.visibility ('visibility distance (fog, dust, smoke)') below the sight distance the road offers at the subject's place (st.sight_distance, which is 'Not a stand-in for ... the clarity of the air (env.visibility)': the two are compared, never substituted).

operationalizations.standard: special hazards by reason of other highway conditions (the catch-all of the standard)
operationalizations.convention: AASHTO stopping-distance model: a highway condition is a special hazard where an obstruction (st.obstruction, 'a physical object on or beside the roadway that is not a road user') lies within the subject's stopping distance D (the s4 model) of its body, the ground distance read through st.region_geometry, or where works or a closure are marked by dev.temporary_traffic_control ('cones, barricades, temporary signs and flashers marking works, a closure or an obstruction') governing (dev.governs) a travel region the subject occupies (rel.occupies, st.travel_region).

operationalizations.standard: the duty to decrease speed: the speed to which the driver must come where a condition of the line holds
operationalizations.convention: AASHTO stopping-sight-distance model and curve side-friction model: the stopping distance D = v times p.driver_reaction_time plus v squared over twice the surface deceleration (p.following_decel_ice on ice or snow, else p.following_decel_wet on a wet road or in precipitation, else p.following_decel_dry) must not exceed the sight distance at the subject's place, nor the visibility where it is shorter, nor the surface gap to a road user in predicted conflict; on a bend v squared times the curvature must not exceed p.curve_lateral_accel_max. The bound moves with the speed, the surface, the sight, the visibility, the curvature and the gap.

operationalizations.standard: special hazards exist or may exist
operationalizations.convention: Traffic-conflict technique: a hazard exists with respect to a road user whose centre comes within p.conflict_centre_clearance of the subject's within p.conflict_horizon under constant velocities; a hazard may exist where a pedestrian occupies a roadway; by reason of weather where rain or snow falls, the road is wet, icy or snow-covered, or the visibility is below the sight distance at the subject's place; by reason of highway conditions where an obstruction lies within the subject's stopping distance (the s4 model) or a temporary traffic-control device governs the subject's region.

residues.why: The words say a speed below the posted limits does not relieve the duty; the duty is the same whether the speed is below or above the limits, so the clause imposes no observable condition.

applicability: The subject is a vehicle (ru.aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle) and, at the observation, at least one condition holds: (a) it occupies an intersection, or a travel region whose entrance end is an intersection; (b) it occupies a roadway whose curvature at its place exceeds p.curvature_resolution, or does so at some observation within the next p.curve_approach_reach of distance it travels (a .path window ahead); (c) a crest lies ahead of its velocity within p.crest_near_reach of its body; (d) it occupies a lane on a highway whose width is at or below p.narrow_lane_width or whose roadway curvature at its place exceeds p.curvature_resolution; (e) a pedestrian occupies a roadway, or some traffic road user other than the subject has a closest approach to it within p.conflict_horizon at a centre distance at or below p.conflict_centre_clearance; (f) rain or snow falls, the road is wet, icy or snow-covered, or the visibility is below the sight distance at its place; (g) an obstruction lies within the stopping distance D of its body, or a temporary traffic-control device governs a travel region it occupies.
obligation: At every such observation the subject's speed v keeps its stopping distance D = v*p.driver_reaction_time + v*v/(2*a), with a = p.following_decel_ice where the road is icy or snow-covered, else p.following_decel_wet where it is wet or rain or snow falls, else p.following_decel_dry, at or below the sight distance at its place and at or below the visibility; where the roadway curvature at its place exceeds p.curvature_resolution, v*v*curvature is at or below p.curve_lateral_accel_max; and for every road user in predicted conflict (condition e), D is at or below the surface gap between the two bodies. Otherwise the duty is violated.

narrowings.why: 'a driver' is read through the vehicle's controlled motion: the duty binds the vehicle's speed whoever or whatever controls it.

'decrease speed' is read as reaching the speed the condition requires (stopping within the sight distance, the visibility and the gap to a road user in conflict; the curve's lateral acceleration bound), not as a deceleration act of a set amount: a vehicle already at such a speed complies.
The catch-all 'other highway conditions' is read only through obstructions within the stopping distance and temporary traffic-control devices governing the subject's region.
Hazards that 'may exist' are read only through a pedestrian on a roadway; other potential hazards are not read.

scenarios.name: forbid
scenarios.narrative: A car occupies a lane that enters an intersection on a dry, straight roadway with no precipitation; the sight distance at its place is 40 m and the visibility is long; it travels at 20 m/s, so its stopping distance at the dry deceleration exceeds 40 m.

scenarios.name: permit
scenarios.narrative: The same approach at 10 m/s: the stopping distance at the dry deceleration is below the 40 m sight distance and the visibility; no road user is in conflict.

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.narrative: A car travels on a dry, straight, wide-laned roadway between intersections, no crest ahead within reach, no pedestrian on the roadway, no road user in conflict, no obstruction or temporary traffic control, visibility longer than the sight distance.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: As in forbid, but the source does not observe the sight distance at the car's place; the curvature is zero and no road user is in conflict, so the verdict turns on the unobserved sight distance.

scenarios.name: branch_1
scenarios.narrative: A car on a roadway with curvature 0.01 1/m (a 100 m radius) at 20 m/s on a dry road with long sight distance: v squared times curvature exceeds the curve lateral-acceleration bound.

scenarios.name: branch_2
scenarios.narrative: A car approaches an intersection at 13 m/s on an icy road with a 60 m sight distance: its stopping distance at the ice deceleration exceeds 60 m, though at the dry deceleration it would not.

scenarios.name: branch_3
scenarios.narrative: A car on a dry straight road at 15 m/s with long sight distance; a pedestrian ahead walks so that its centre comes within the conflict clearance of the car's within the conflict horizon, and the surface gap is 20 m, shorter than the car's stopping distance.

param_proposals.name: p.driver_reaction_time
param_proposals.convention: perception-reaction time of an alert driver to an expected hazard in the stopping-distance model
param_proposals.source: AASHTO A Policy on Geometric Design of Highways and Streets, stopping sight distance

param_proposals.name: p.following_decel_dry
param_proposals.convention: braking deceleration of a passenger vehicle on a dry paved surface (coefficient of friction about 0.6)
param_proposals.source: vehicle braking friction tables (accident reconstruction practice)

param_proposals.name: p.following_decel_wet
param_proposals.convention: braking deceleration of a passenger vehicle on a wet paved surface (coefficient of friction about 0.4)
param_proposals.source: vehicle braking friction tables (accident reconstruction practice)

param_proposals.name: p.following_decel_ice
param_proposals.convention: braking deceleration of a passenger vehicle on an icy or snow-covered surface (coefficient of friction about 0.1)
param_proposals.source: vehicle braking friction tables (accident reconstruction practice)

param_proposals.name: p.curve_lateral_accel_max
param_proposals.convention: the lateral acceleration a passenger vehicle sustains on a curve within comfortable side friction on a dry or wet paved surface (about 0.3 g)
param_proposals.source: AASHTO Green Book horizontal curve side-friction factors

param_proposals.name: p.curvature_resolution
param_proposals.convention: the horizontal curvature at or below which a mapped roadway reads as straight: the curvature resolution of map centrelines (a radius of about two kilometres)
param_proposals.source: HD map centreline accuracy

param_proposals.name: p.curve_approach_reach
param_proposals.convention: the distance a road user travels ahead within which a bend it reaches counts as one it is approaching: about the stopping sight distance at 90 km/h, the distance over which a driver must already be slowing for the bend
param_proposals.source: AASHTO Green Book stopping sight distance and horizontal curve warning placement (MUTCD Table 2C-4)

param_proposals.name: p.crest_near_reach
param_proposals.convention: the ground distance from a road user's body to a crest within which the road user is on the approach to or near the crest: the length of a crest vertical curve over which forward sight is restricted, about the stopping sight distance at 90 km/h
param_proposals.source: AASHTO Green Book crest vertical curves and stopping sight distance

param_proposals.name: p.narrow_lane_width
param_proposals.convention: the lane width at or below which a highway's lane counts as narrow: below the 3.3 to 3.6 m design lane width at which a passenger car and a truck meet with comfortable lateral clearance
param_proposals.source: AASHTO Green Book, lane width

param_proposals.name: p.conflict_horizon
param_proposals.convention: time-to-collision threshold of the traffic-conflict technique: a closest approach later than this is not a present danger of a crash
param_proposals.source: traffic conflict technique (Hyden; time-to-collision thresholds)

param_proposals.name: p.conflict_centre_clearance
param_proposals.convention: centre-to-centre distance at the closest approach below which the bodies of a passenger car and another road user are taken to collide or nearly collide: about a car's half-length plus half a body width
param_proposals.source: passenger car design dimensions

segmentation.text: The fact that the speed of a vehicle is lower than the prescribed limits
does not relieve
a driver
from the duty to decrease speed
when approaching and crossing an intersection,
when approaching and going around a curve,
when approaching a hill crest,
when traveling upon any narrow or winding highway,
or when special hazards exist or may exist
with respect to pedestrians or other traffic,
or by reason of weather
or other highway conditions,
and speed must be decreased
as may be necessary to avoid colliding
with any person, vehicle or other conveyance
on or entering a highway
in compliance with legal requirements and the duty of all persons to use due care.

elements.justification: 'a driver' is, by DEF-NRS-484A-080, 'every person who drives or is in actual physical control of a vehicle': the duty binds the vehicle the driver controls, the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle. ru.aggregate is 'membership of a legal aggregate', not the relational role of driving, which is read through the vehicle's controlled motion (observable_reading agency).

Speed decreased: the subject's kin.speed ('magnitude of velocity') falling, observed as kin.accel_longitudinal ('acceleration along heading, signed') at or below minus p.speed_decrease_decel_min; kin.accel_longitudinal is 'Not a stand-in for: speed', and speed is read from kin.speed itself.

The parties are 'any person, vehicle or other conveyance': the vehicle word claims its admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle; persons (afoot or riding) and other conveyances cover every other road user, so the union leaves no class out and the rule quantifies over every road user of the scene other than the subject, whatever its class; the aggregate restricts nothing. Colliding with one is rel.contact, 'the bodies of two road users ... touch or overlap (a collision)', 'Not a stand-in for: a near miss'.

The other road user is on or entering a highway: its footprint overlaps (rel.occupies, 'a road user's footprint overlaps a lane / region') a highway region (st.highway, 'the entire public way between its boundary lines, including sidewalks and shoulders', 'Not a stand-in for: the roadway': the words name the whole highway, so the whole highway is read). A road user entering the highway overlaps it from the observation its footprint reaches it.

operationalizations.standard: speed decreased as may be necessary to avoid colliding
operationalizations.convention: Traffic-conflict technique: a collision is to be avoided with a road user whose centre comes within p.conflict_centre_clearance of the subject's within p.conflict_horizon under constant velocities; the speed is being decreased where the longitudinal acceleration is at or below minus p.speed_decrease_decel_min, the source's acceleration resolution, or the subject is at rest (speed at or below p.halt_speed_tolerance); contact while the subject moves is a collision not avoided.

operationalizations.standard: in compliance with legal requirements and the duty of all persons to use due care
operationalizations.convention: AASHTO stopping-distance model: due care is met toward a road user in predicted conflict where the subject's stopping distance D = v times p.driver_reaction_time plus v squared over twice the surface deceleration (p.following_decel_ice on ice or snow, else p.following_decel_wet on a wet road or in precipitation, else p.following_decel_dry) is at or below the surface gap between the bodies; the bound moves with speed, surface and gap.

applicability: The subject is a vehicle (ru.aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle).
obligation: For every road user u of the scene other than the subject that occupies a highway and whose closest approach to the subject lies within p.conflict_horizon at a centre distance at or below p.conflict_centre_clearance: the subject is at rest (speed at or below p.halt_speed_tolerance), or its longitudinal acceleration is at or below minus p.speed_decrease_decel_min, or its stopping distance D = v*p.driver_reaction_time + v*v/(2*a) (a = p.following_decel_ice on ice or snow, else p.following_decel_wet where wet or precipitating, else p.following_decel_dry) is at or below the surface gap between the two bodies. And for every road user u other than the subject occupying a highway, the subject is not in contact with u while its speed exceeds p.halt_speed_tolerance. Otherwise violated; with no such road user the subject complies.

narrowings.why: 'a driver' is read through the vehicle's controlled motion: the duty binds the vehicle's speed whoever or whatever controls it.

'in compliance with legal requirements' is read as qualifying how the speed must be decreased and is read only through the due-care stopping-distance bound; other legal requirements are judged by their own rules, not here.
Avoidance is read through the predicted closest approach of centres under constant velocities and actual contact; a conflict the constant-velocity prediction does not show is not read.

scenarios.name: forbid
scenarios.narrative: A car at 15 m/s on a dry road holds its speed (zero longitudinal acceleration) while a pedestrian entering the highway ahead is predicted to come within the conflict clearance within the conflict horizon; the surface gap is 15 m, shorter than the car's stopping distance.

scenarios.name: permit
scenarios.narrative: The same scene, but the car brakes at 4 m/s^2, its longitudinal acceleration below minus the decrease threshold.

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.narrative: The subject is a pedestrian walking on a sidewalk; it is no vehicle.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: As in forbid, but the source does not supply the surface gap between the bodies; the car holds its speed, so whether its stopping distance fits the gap is unobserved.

scenarios.name: branch_1
scenarios.narrative: The car is alone on the highway at 25 m/s: no other road user is in the scene, so the duty is decided for the subject alone and met.

scenarios.name: branch_2
scenarios.narrative: The car, moving at 5 m/s, touches a cyclist on the highway (rel.contact true).

param_proposals.name: p.conflict_horizon
param_proposals.convention: time-to-collision threshold of the traffic-conflict technique: a closest approach later than this is not a present danger of a crash
param_proposals.source: traffic conflict technique (Hyden; time-to-collision thresholds)

param_proposals.name: p.conflict_centre_clearance

param_proposals.name: p.speed_decrease_decel_min

param_proposals.name: p.halt_speed_tolerance

param_proposals.source: speed resolution of the acquisition source

param_proposals.name: p.driver_reaction_time
param_proposals.convention: perception-reaction time of an alert driver to an expected hazard in the stopping-distance model
param_proposals.source: AASHTO A Policy on Geometric Design of Highways and Streets, stopping sight distance

param_proposals.name: p.following_decel_dry
param_proposals.convention: braking deceleration of a passenger vehicle on a dry paved surface (coefficient of friction about 0.6)
param_proposals.source: vehicle braking friction tables (accident reconstruction practice)

param_proposals.name: p.following_decel_wet
param_proposals.convention: braking deceleration of a passenger vehicle on a wet paved surface (coefficient of friction about 0.4)
param_proposals.source: vehicle braking friction tables (accident reconstruction practice)

segmentation.text: After the establishment of a speed zone and the installation of appropriate signs to control speed,
it is unlawful for any person to drive a motor vehicle
upon the road
and in the speed zone
in excess of the speed therein authorized.

elements.justification: The established speed zone and its installed signs are read by their presence: dev.zone_sign of kind speed_zone, 'a sign that begins or ends a signed zone along the road', and dev.speed_limit_sign, 'sign stating a maximum or minimum speed, with value and unit; kind ∈ {maximum, minimum, structure_maximum, zone}', both governing (dev.governs, 'the travel regions whose traffic the device controls') the travel region the subject occupies (rel.occupies, st.travel_region). dev.zone_sign is 'Not a stand-in for: whether the condition holds now'; no posted conditions are read here, the zone sign's presence is the zone. The establishment by an authority is a status read from the signs (observable_reading status).

'motor vehicle' is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-130::motor_vehicle ('every vehicle which is self-propelled but not operated upon rails. The term does not include an electric bicycle or an electric scooter'); ru.aggregate is 'membership of a legal aggregate'. 'any person to drive' is read through the vehicle's controlled motion (observable_reading agency).

In the speed zone: the subject's footprint overlaps (rel.occupies) a travel region (st.travel_region) that a dev.zone_sign of kind speed_zone, not marking the zone's end, governs (dev.governs) and that lies on a highway (st.on_way, 'the public way (a highway region) a structure region lies on'; st.highway): the road of DEF-NRS-484A-215 is 'the entire width between the boundary lines of every highway' outside a city, whose observable part is the highway.

The speed therein authorized is the value of a dev.speed_limit_sign of kind zone or maximum ('sign stating a maximum or minimum speed, with value and unit') governing a travel region the subject occupies; in excess is kin.speed ('magnitude of velocity', m/s) above that value.

applicability: The subject is a motor vehicle (ru.aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-130::motor_vehicle); its place is not within an incorporated city (the assumption asm.within_incorporated_city is declared false: a road is, by DEF-NRS-484A-215, a highway 'outside the territorial limits of a city'); and it occupies a travel region r lying on a highway that is governed by a zone sign of kind speed_zone (not an end sign) and by a speed limit sign of kind zone or maximum.
obligation: Re-binding every travel region the subject occupies that lies on a highway and is governed by a zone sign of kind speed_zone (not an end sign), the subject's speed is at or below the value of every speed limit sign of kind zone or maximum governing that region. A speed above such a value is violated.

narrowings.why: The establishment of the zone and the installation of its signs by an authority are read from the presence of the speed-zone sign and the speed limit sign governing the subject's region.
'any person to drive' is read through the motor vehicle's controlled motion, whoever or whatever controls it.
The speed 'therein authorized' is read as the value of a speed limit sign of kind zone or maximum governing the subject's region; a minimum speed sign authorizes no maximum and is not read.

scenarios.name: forbid
scenarios.narrative: A car outside any incorporated city (asm.within_incorporated_city false) occupies a lane on a highway governed by a speed_zone zone sign and a zone speed limit sign of 20 m/s; its speed is 25 m/s.

scenarios.name: permit
scenarios.narrative: The same scene with the car at 18 m/s.

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.narrative: A car outside any city on a highway lane that no speed_zone zone sign governs; only a general maximum speed sign is present.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: As in forbid, but the source does not supply the car's speed.

scenarios.name: branch_1
scenarios.narrative: As in forbid, but the reading declares the place within an incorporated city (asm.within_incorporated_city true): it is no road.

segmentation.text: If any driver or operator of a motor vehicle
drives or operates a motor vehicle
at a speed so slow as to impede the forward movement of
traffic proceeding immediately behind the driver or operator,
the driver or operator shall:
If the highway has one lane for traveling in each direction
and the width of the paved portion permits,
drive to the extreme right side of the highway
and, if applicable, comply with the provisions of NRS 484B.630.

elements.justification: 'motor vehicle' is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-130::motor_vehicle ('every vehicle which is self-propelled but not operated upon rails'); 'driver or operator' is read through the vehicle's controlled motion (observable_reading agency), never as membership.

Drives or operates a motor vehicle: the motor vehicle (admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-130::motor_vehicle) is moving, its kin.speed ('magnitude of velocity') above p.halt_speed_tolerance; a vehicle moving on the road is taken to be driven (observable_reading agency).

'traffic' is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-285::traffic ('pedestrians, ridden or herded animals, vehicles and other conveyances ... using any highway for purposes of travel'). Proceeding immediately behind: a traffic road user t with the subject ahead of it in the same lane (rel.ahead_behind_in_lane, 'a is ahead of / behind b in the same lane, along the lane direction') and the gap between the bodies (rel.surface_gap, 'distance between the nearest points of two bodies') within p.rear_signal_reach; the surface gap, not rel.centre_distance, which is 'Not a stand-in for: a clearance between bodies'.

'the driver or operator' refers back to the motor vehicle's driver of u1: the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-130::motor_vehicle, read through the vehicle's controlled motion (observable_reading agency).

The subject occupies (rel.occupies) a lane (st.lane) lying on a highway (st.on_way, st.highway) whose count of lanes in its direction (st.lane_adjacency, 'lane ordinal within the carriageway and the count of lanes in that direction') is the stated one; and the other direction: some lane on the same highway whose designated direction (st.lane_direction, 'direction of travel designated for a structure a vehicle travels in') is opposed to the subject's lane's (the dot product of the two normalised directions below minus p.lane_opposed_direction_cos), and every such opposed lane's count in its direction is also the stated one. Reuses the atoms of the index mapping 'upon highways having width for not more than one line of traffic in each direction' (NRS_484B_203_1_o2), with the lane direction added to tell the two directions apart; st.lane_adjacency is 'Not a stand-in for: the marking between two lanes', which is not read.

The extreme right side is the right-hand edge of the roadway (st.road_edge, 'curb or edge of the roadway') lying on the highway the subject occupies (st.on_way, st.highway, rel.occupies), its boundary from st.region_geometry. The subject's right body side is within p.pullover_edge_gap of that edge: the edge's lateral offset from the subject (prim.region_lateral_offset, 'the signed lateral offset ... of a structure region from a road user', negative to the right) in magnitude, less half the subject's width (kin.extent, 'a formula reads the full length, width and height').

operationalizations.standard: so slow as to impede the forward movement of traffic
operationalizations.convention: Slow-moving-vehicle practice: the subject impedes the traffic behind it where, at every observation of the window of p.left_lane_move_over_time behind (the time a driver needs to check, signal and move over once a faster vehicle closes), it moves (speed above p.halt_speed_tolerance) at a speed more than p.impeding_speed_margin below the value of a maximum speed limit sign governing a travel region it occupies, a traffic road user is behind it in the same lane within p.rear_signal_reach, and no road user is ahead of it in the same lane within p.rear_signal_reach, so the subject is not itself held back.

operationalizations.standard: the width of the paved portion permits
operationalizations.convention: Lateral clearance of a passing vehicle: the paved half of the roadway, from the centre line to the right road edge (the sum of the magnitudes of their lateral offsets from the subject), is at least the subject's width plus p.free_passage_width, so that with the subject at the right edge a following vehicle has room to pass beside it.

residues.why: NRS 484B.630 has no node in the library, so its turnout duty cannot be composed; the rule does not judge compliance with it.

applicability: The subject is a motor vehicle and, at every observation of the window of p.left_lane_move_over_time behind the judged observation, it moves (speed above p.halt_speed_tolerance), its speed plus p.impeding_speed_margin is below the value of a maximum speed limit sign governing a travel region it occupies, some traffic road user is behind it in the same lane with the surface gap within p.rear_signal_reach, and no road user is ahead of it in the same lane within p.rear_signal_reach; at the judged observation it occupies a lane on a highway whose lane count in its direction is one, some lane on the same highway has a designated direction opposed to it (dot product below minus p.lane_opposed_direction_cos) and every such opposed lane's count in its direction is one, and the magnitude of the centre line's lateral offset plus that of the right road edge's is at least its width plus p.free_passage_width.
obligation: At the judged observation the magnitude of the lateral offset of the right-hand road edge of the highway it occupies, less half the subject's width, is at or below p.pullover_edge_gap: its right side is at the extreme right of the roadway. Otherwise violated.

narrowings.why: 'driver or operator' is read through the motor vehicle's controlled motion, whoever or whatever controls it.
'drives or operates' is read as the motor vehicle moving under control: a vehicle moving on the road is taken to be driven.
'the driver or operator' binds the motor vehicle's conduct whoever controls it.

'so slow as to impede' is read against the posted maximum governing the subject's region and through traffic in the same lane immediately behind, sustained over the move-over time; where no maximum speed sign governs the subject's region the reference speed is unobserved and the duty is unknown.

'the extreme right side of the highway' is read as the right edge of the roadway: the subject is not required to enter a shoulder, and its right side within p.pullover_edge_gap of that edge counts as at the extreme right.

segmentation.text: If any driver or operator of a motor vehicle
drives or operates a motor vehicle
at a speed so slow as to impede the forward movement of
traffic proceeding immediately behind the driver or operator,
the driver or operator shall:
If the highway has two or more clearly marked lanes for traffic traveling in the direction in which the driver or operator is traveling,
drive in the extreme right-hand lane
except when necessary
to pass other slowly moving vehicles.

elements.justification: 'motor vehicle' is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-130::motor_vehicle ('every vehicle which is self-propelled but not operated upon rails'); 'driver or operator' is read through the vehicle's controlled motion (observable_reading agency), never as membership.

Drives or operates a motor vehicle: the motor vehicle (admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-130::motor_vehicle) is moving, its kin.speed ('magnitude of velocity') above p.halt_speed_tolerance; a vehicle moving on the road is taken to be driven (observable_reading agency).

'traffic' is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-285::traffic. Proceeding immediately behind: a traffic road user t with the subject ahead of it in the same lane (rel.ahead_behind_in_lane, 'a is ahead of / behind b in the same lane, along the lane direction') and the gap between the bodies (rel.surface_gap, 'distance between the nearest points of two bodies') within p.rear_signal_reach.

'the driver or operator' refers back to the motor vehicle's driver of u1: the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-130::motor_vehicle, read through the vehicle's controlled motion (observable_reading agency).

Reuses the index mapping of 'If a highway has two or more clearly marked lanes for traffic traveling in one direction,' (NRS_484B_223_1b: rel.occupies, ru.aggregate traffic, st.lane, st.lane_adjacency) with the highway anchor added: the subject occupies a lane (st.lane) on a highway (st.on_way, st.highway) whose count of lanes in that lane's direction (st.lane_adjacency, 'the count of lanes in that direction') is at least the stated two; the lane the subject occupies carries its direction of travel. 'traffic' is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-285::traffic, named here only as the users of the lanes. The clear marking is read from the mapped lanes' presence (observable_reading status).

The extreme right-hand lane is the lane whose ordinal equals the count of lanes in its direction: st.lane_adjacency gives 'lane ordinal within the carriageway and the count of lanes in that direction; ordinal 1 is the leftmost lane, looking along the lane's direction'. The subject's footprint overlaps it (rel.occupies) and no other lane of that direction; lane membership is not a lateral offset, as st.lane's 'Not a stand-in for' requires.

Other slowly moving vehicles: a road user v of the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle, moving (kin.speed above p.halt_speed_tolerance) slower than the subject, on the subject's right (rel.bearing, 'direction of b from a in a's frame', its lateral component negative), and either side by side with it (rel.longitudinal_overlap, 'the length the two footprints' projections on that axis share', at or above zero) or ahead of it (bearing's longitudinal component positive) at a body gap (rel.surface_gap) the operationalization of v8 bounds.

operationalizations.standard: so slow as to impede the forward movement of traffic
operationalizations.convention: Slow-moving-vehicle practice: the subject impedes the traffic behind it where, at every observation of the window of p.left_lane_move_over_time behind (the time a driver needs to check, signal and move over once a faster vehicle closes), it moves (speed above p.halt_speed_tolerance) at a speed more than p.impeding_speed_margin below the value of a maximum speed limit sign governing a travel region it occupies, a traffic road user is behind it in the same lane within p.rear_signal_reach, and no road user is ahead of it in the same lane within p.rear_signal_reach.

Overtaking duration: passing a slower vehicle is necessary while the subject is side by side with it, or while it is ahead at a body gap the subject closes within p.overtake_window at their speed difference (gap at or below the speed difference times p.overtake_window); the bound moves with the closing speed.

applicability: The subject is a motor vehicle and, at every observation of the window of p.left_lane_move_over_time behind the judged observation, it moves (speed above p.halt_speed_tolerance), its speed plus p.impeding_speed_margin is below the value of a maximum speed limit sign governing a travel region it occupies, some traffic road user is behind it in the same lane with the surface gap within p.rear_signal_reach, and no road user is ahead of it in the same lane within p.rear_signal_reach; at the judged observation it occupies a lane on a highway whose count of lanes in that lane's direction is two or more.
obligation: The subject occupies the lane of its direction whose ordinal equals the lane count, and no other lane of that direction; except where some vehicle (DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle) other than the subject, moving above p.halt_speed_tolerance and slower than the subject, lies on its right (lateral bearing component negative) and is either side by side with it (longitudinal overlap at or above zero) or ahead of it at a surface gap at or below (subject speed minus its speed) times p.overtake_window. Otherwise violated.

narrowings.why: 'driver or operator' is read through the motor vehicle's controlled motion, whoever or whatever controls it.
'drives or operates' is read as the motor vehicle moving under control.
'the driver or operator' binds the motor vehicle's conduct whoever controls it.
'clearly marked' lanes are read from the mapped lanes' presence; the paint's clarity is not modelled.

'so slow as to impede' is read against the posted maximum governing the subject's region and through traffic in the same lane immediately behind, sustained over the move-over time; where no maximum speed sign governs the subject's region the reference speed is unobserved and the duty is unknown.

segmentation.text: If any driver or operator of a motor vehicle
drives or operates a motor vehicle
at a speed so slow as to impede the forward movement of
traffic proceeding immediately behind the driver or operator,
the driver or operator shall:
If the highway is a controlled-access highway,
use alternate routes whenever possible.

elements.justification: 'motor vehicle' is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-130::motor_vehicle; 'driver or operator' is read through the vehicle's controlled motion (observable_reading agency), never as membership.

Drives or operates a motor vehicle: the motor vehicle (admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-130::motor_vehicle) is moving, its kin.speed ('magnitude of velocity') above p.halt_speed_tolerance (observable_reading agency).

'traffic' is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-285::traffic. Proceeding immediately behind: a traffic road user with the subject ahead of it in the same lane (rel.ahead_behind_in_lane) and the gap between bodies (rel.surface_gap, 'distance between the nearest points of two bodies') within p.rear_signal_reach.
'the driver or operator' refers back to the motor vehicle of u1, read through its controlled motion (observable_reading agency).

Reuses the index mapping of 'on a controlled-access highway' (NRS_484B_208_1): the subject's footprint overlaps (rel.occupies) a st.controlled_access region, 'a highway with access only at designated points, and its entrance and exit lanes', which is what DEF-NRS-484A-060 states ('no legal right of access except at such points only').

Nearest atoms only: being on the controlled-access highway (rel.occupies, st.controlled_access) shows the subject is not on an alternate route, but no atom says whether an alternate route exists for the subject's trip, which decides whether using one is possible. See the gap.

operationalizations.standard: so slow as to impede the forward movement of traffic
operationalizations.convention: Slow-moving-vehicle practice: the subject impedes the traffic behind it where, at every observation of the window of p.left_lane_move_over_time behind, it moves (speed above p.halt_speed_tolerance) at a speed more than p.impeding_speed_margin below the value of a maximum speed limit sign governing a travel region it occupies, a traffic road user is behind it in the same lane within p.rear_signal_reach, and no road user is ahead of it in the same lane within p.rear_signal_reach.

applicability: The subject is a motor vehicle that has impeded the traffic immediately behind it over the window of p.left_lane_move_over_time (as in the u3 operationalization) and occupies a controlled-access highway.
obligation: The subject does not travel on the controlled-access highway where an alternate route exists for its trip between the place it entered and the place it leaves that highway (the missing atom of the gap); where none exists the duty is met.

narrowings.why: 'driver or operator' is read through the motor vehicle's controlled motion, whoever or whatever controls it.
'drives or operates' is read as the motor vehicle moving under control.
'the driver or operator' binds the motor vehicle's conduct whoever controls it.

gaps.proposal: `st.alternate_route` | relation: for a road user on a controlled-access highway, a way of the road network other than a controlled-access highway, open to the road user's class, that connects the place at which the road user entered that highway with the place at which it leaves it, as the map's routing records; true where such a way exists **Not a stand-in for:** the road user's destination or plan, nor a road's speed, capacity or congestion | general
gaps.nearest: rel.occupies, st.controlled_access: they show the road user is on a controlled-access highway and so not on an alternate route, but not whether an alternate route to the same place exists, which decides whether the duty to use one can be carried out ('whenever possible').

segmentation.text: A person
shall not bring a vehicle to a complete stop
upon a roadway
so as to impede or block the normal and reasonable movement of
traffic
unless the stop is necessary
for safe operation
or in compliance with law.

elements.justification: Reuses the index mapping of 'A person' (LVMC_11_22_010): the person who brings a vehicle to a stop is read through the vehicle's controlled motion (observable_reading agency); the class is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle, 'membership of a legal aggregate', not the role of driving.

A complete stop is the concept drv.motion.complete_halt: 'The road user is at rest at the observation — "complete cessation from movement" — observed as its speed (kin.speed) at or below a tolerance the caller sets', filled with p.halt_speed_tolerance. Of the two stop definitions the run leaves ambiguous, DEF-NRS-484A-255 ('complete cessation from movement') and DEF-NRS-484A-260 ('any halting, even momentarily'), both denote this halt; the concept says nothing of how long the vehicle stays at rest, so a momentary halt is read too. 'a vehicle' is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle.

Upon a roadway: the subject's footprint overlaps (rel.occupies) a st.roadway, 'the part of a highway improved for vehicular traffic, excluding shoulder', which is DEF-NRS-484A-220 ('improved and ordinarily used for vehicular traffic, exclusive of the shoulder'); 'Not a stand-in for: the sidewalk' — a halt on the shoulder or in a bay is not on the roadway.

'traffic' is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-285::traffic ('pedestrians, ridden or herded animals, vehicles and other conveyances ... using any highway for purposes of travel'); the traffic whose movement is impeded is a traffic road user behind the subject in the same lane (rel.ahead_behind_in_lane) at a body gap (rel.surface_gap) the operationalization of x4 bounds.

Safe operation requires the stop where the subject halts behind a road user ahead of it in the same lane (rel.ahead_behind_in_lane) within a queue gap between bodies (rel.surface_gap), or where some road user is predicted to come close to it (prim.closest_approach_within, prim.closest_approach_distance; 'Not a stand-in for ... the danger of a crash' alone, the bound being the operationalization of x6).

Extends the index mapping of 'or in compliance with law' (NRS_484B_450_1a: dev.governs, dev.stop_sign, dev.traffic_signal, rel.occupies, st.travel_region) with the other controls whose indication requires a halt, as the mapping of 'shall not: Stop, stand or park a vehicle' (NRS_484B_477_1a) reads them: a stop sign (dev.stop_sign, 'regulatory sign requiring a full halt'), a yield sign (dev.yield_sign, 'requiring yielding without a mandatory halt', where a halt is how the yield is given), a traffic signal showing circular_red, a red_arrow or flashing_red (dev.traffic_signal), a person directing traffic with indication stop (dev.human_direction, role police_officer, flagger, school_crossing_guard or railroad_flagger), or railway lights flashing or a gate not up (dev.railway_signal_or_gate), governing (dev.governs) a travel region the subject occupies (rel.occupies, st.travel_region). dev.governs is 'Not a stand-in for: a position', and no position is read from it.

operationalizations.standard: so as to impede or block the normal and reasonable movement of traffic
operationalizations.convention: Queue convention: the halt impedes or blocks traffic where a traffic road user is behind the halted subject in the same lane with the gap between bodies within p.rear_signal_reach (immediately to the rear) and that road user is itself at rest (complete halt within p.halt_speed_tolerance: blocked) or decelerating at p.speed_decrease_decel_min or more (impeded).

operationalizations.standard: the stop is necessary for safe operation
operationalizations.convention: Queue spacing and the traffic-conflict technique: the stop is necessary where a road user is ahead of the subject in the same lane with the body gap within p.queue_halt_gap (the subject halts behind other traffic), or where some road user's centre is predicted to come within p.conflict_centre_clearance of the subject's within p.conflict_horizon.

applicability: The subject is a vehicle (DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle) occupying a roadway.
obligation: Violated where the subject is at rest (drv.motion.complete_halt with p.halt_speed_tolerance) and some traffic road user other than the subject is behind it in the same lane with the body gap within p.rear_signal_reach and is at rest or decelerating at p.speed_decrease_decel_min or more; except where (a) some road user is ahead of the subject in the same lane with the body gap within p.queue_halt_gap, or some road user's closest approach to the subject lies within p.conflict_horizon at a centre distance at or below p.conflict_centre_clearance, or (b) a control requiring a halt governs a travel region the subject occupies: a stop sign, a yield sign, a traffic signal showing circular_red, a red_arrow or flashing_red, a person directing traffic with indication stop, or railway crossing lights flashing or a gate not up. A moving subject, or one halted with no traffic held behind it, complies.

narrowings.why: 'A person' who brings the vehicle to a stop is read through the vehicle's controlled motion, whoever or whatever controls it.
'the normal and reasonable movement of traffic' is read only through traffic behind the subject in its own lane, halted or decelerating; traffic in other lanes is not read.

segmentation.text: It is unlawful for any person to drive a vehicle
over any bridge or other elevated structure constituting a part of a highway
at a speed which is greater than the maximum speed which can be maintained with safety to the bridge or structure,
when such structure is signposted as provided in this section
[(3) appended below].

The Department of Transportation upon request from any local authority shall, or upon its own initiative may, conduct an investigation of any bridge or other elevated structure constituting a part of a highway constructed and maintained under the authority granted by chapter 408 of NRS,
and if it thereupon finds that such structure cannot with safety to itself withstand vehicles traveling at the speed otherwise permissible under chapters 484A to 484E, inclusive, of NRS,
the Department shall determine and declare the maximum speed of vehicles which such structure can safely withstand,
and shall cause or permit suitable signs stating such maximum speed to be erected and maintained
at a distance of 100 feet before each end of such structure.

elements.justification: 'vehicle' is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle ('every device in, upon or by which any person or property is or may be transported or drawn upon a highway'); ru.aggregate is 'membership of a legal aggregate'. 'any person to drive' is read through the vehicle's controlled motion (observable_reading agency).

Driving over a bridge or other elevated structure: the subject's footprint overlaps (rel.occupies) a st.elevated_structure, 'bridge, viaduct or tunnel carrying the roadway', that lies on a highway (st.on_way, 'the public way (a highway region) a structure region lies on'; st.highway) — the structure 'constituting a part of a highway'.

The maximum speed which can be maintained with safety to the structure is the one the sign states: the value of a dev.speed_limit_sign of kind structure_maximum ('sign stating a maximum or minimum speed, with value and unit') governing (dev.governs) a travel region the subject occupies (rel.occupies, st.travel_region) while on the structure; greater than is kin.speed ('magnitude of velocity') above that value. The safety of the structure is the authority's determination (y8), not a judgement left to the driver, so the span is no standard.

Signposted: a dev.speed_limit_sign of kind structure_maximum governs (dev.governs, 'the travel regions whose traffic the device controls') a travel region the subject occupies (rel.occupies, st.travel_region) while on the structure; 'as provided in this section' is read from the sign's presence (observable_reading status). dev.governs is 'Not a stand-in for: a position', so the sign's distance from the structure is not read from it.

The suitable signs stating such maximum speed are dev.speed_limit_sign of kind structure_maximum, whose value is the declared maximum; their erection and maintenance are read from their presence and governance (dev.governs) of the structure's travel regions.

residues.why: The authority's investigation, on request or on its own initiative, of structures built under chapter 408 of NRS (outside the corpus) is the process behind the posting; the rule reads the posted sign as the evidence of it.

The authority's finding that the structure cannot withstand the otherwise permissible speeds (chapters 484A to 484E, no node of the corpus) is the reason for the posting; the rule reads the posted maximum, not the finding.
The authority's determination and declaration of the maximum speed is read through the value the posted sign states; the act of declaring is not observable.

The sign's placement before each end of the structure is the authority's duty; the rule reads the sign's governance of the structure's travel regions, not its distance from the ends, so the placement is not checked.

applicability: The subject is a vehicle (DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle) occupying an elevated structure that lies on a highway, and a speed limit sign of kind structure_maximum governs a travel region the subject occupies.
obligation: Re-binding every speed limit sign of kind structure_maximum governing a travel region the subject occupies while it occupies an elevated structure on a highway, the subject's speed is at or below that sign's value. Otherwise violated.

narrowings.why: 'any person to drive' is read through the vehicle's controlled motion, whoever or whatever controls it.

'signposted as provided in this section' is read from the presence of a structure-maximum speed sign governing the travel region the subject occupies on the structure; the authority's investigation, declaration and placement are presumed from it.

scenarios.name: forbid
scenarios.narrative: A truck occupies a bridge lying on a highway; a structure_maximum speed sign of 11 m/s governs the bridge lane it occupies; its speed is 16 m/s.

scenarios.name: permit
scenarios.narrative: The same truck on the same bridge at 10 m/s.

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.narrative: A car on a bridge lying on a highway whose lanes no structure_maximum speed sign governs.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: As in forbid, but the source does not observe which regions the speed limit sign governs, so whether the bridge is signposted is unknown.

scenarios.name: branch_1
scenarios.narrative: A car at 16 m/s on an ordinary roadway lane, off any elevated structure, though a structure_maximum sign governs the lane ahead of the bridge.

segmentation.text: It is unlawful for a person to:
Drive a vehicle
in willful or wanton disregard of the safety of persons or property
on a highway
or premises to which the public has access.

elements.justification: The forbidden driving is read through the vehicle's motion: kin.speed ('magnitude of velocity') and kin.accel_longitudinal ('acceleration along heading, signed', 'Not a stand-in for: speed'), the magnitudes the operationalization of d3 bounds.

'vehicle' is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle ('every device in, upon or by which any person or property is or may be transported or drawn upon a highway'); 'Drive' is read through the vehicle's controlled motion (observable_reading agency), never as membership.

Reuses the index mapping of 'on a highway' (LVMC_11_16_090_A_o1): the subject's footprint overlaps (rel.occupies) a st.highway, 'the entire public way between its boundary lines, including sidewalks and shoulders', which is DEF-NRS-484A-095's 'entire width between the boundary lines of every way'; 'Not a stand-in for: the roadway', so the whole highway is read.

operationalizations.standard: willful or wanton disregard of the safety of persons or property
operationalizations.convention: Exhibition-driving and traffic-conflict conventions: the driving shows disregard of the safety of persons or property where the vehicle travels at or above p.exhibition_speed_min (beyond any posted limit), or where it accelerates at p.exhibition_accel_min or more while another road user's centre is predicted to come within p.conflict_centre_clearance of its own within p.conflict_horizon (driving hard into a conflict).

assumptions.meaning: the place of the road user at the observation lies on premises to which the public has access, as the map's reading classifies the area

applicability: The subject is a vehicle (DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle) that occupies a highway, or whose place the reading declares to be premises to which the public has access (asm.public_access_premises).
obligation: Violated where the subject's speed is at or above p.exhibition_speed_min, or where its longitudinal acceleration is at or above p.exhibition_accel_min while some road user other than the subject has a closest approach to it within p.conflict_horizon at a centre distance at or below p.conflict_centre_clearance. Otherwise compliant (a surrogate: its verdicts are evidence, not a legal conclusion on the driver's state of mind).

narrowings.why: 'Drive' is read through the vehicle's controlled motion, whoever or whatever controls it.

'willful or wanton' is a state of mind and is read only through conduct (extreme speed, hard acceleration into a predicted conflict); 'persons or property' is read through other road users and the persons and property they carry; property that is no road user is not read.

scenarios.name: forbid
scenarios.narrative: A car on a highway travels at 50 m/s, above the exhibition speed.

scenarios.name: permit
scenarios.narrative: A car on a highway travels at 15 m/s with gentle acceleration; no road user is in predicted conflict with it.

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.narrative: A car on a private farm way, off any highway, with the reading declaring the place not premises to which the public has access.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: A car on a highway with no other road user in the scene, but the source does not supply its speed.

scenarios.name: branch_1
scenarios.narrative: A car in a public parking lot (asm.public_access_premises true) accelerates at 5 m/s^2 toward a pedestrian whose centre is predicted to come within the conflict clearance within the conflict horizon.

scenarios.name: branch_2
scenarios.narrative: A car alone on a highway at 25 m/s: no other road user in the scene, speed below the exhibition speed.

param_proposals.name: p.exhibition_speed_min
param_proposals.convention: a speed of about 100 mph, beyond any posted limit in the jurisdiction
param_proposals.source: Nevada posted speed limits (maximum 80 mph)

param_proposals.name: p.exhibition_accel_min
param_proposals.convention: harsh-acceleration threshold: a longitudinal acceleration of about 0.4 g, beyond ordinary driving
param_proposals.source: naturalistic driving harsh-event thresholds

param_proposals.name: p.conflict_horizon
param_proposals.convention: time-to-collision threshold of the traffic-conflict technique: a closest approach later than this is not a present danger of a crash
param_proposals.source: traffic conflict technique (Hyden; time-to-collision thresholds)

param_proposals.name: p.conflict_centre_clearance
param_proposals.convention: centre-to-centre distance at the closest approach below which the bodies of a passenger car and another road user are taken to collide or nearly collide: about a car's half-length plus half a body width
param_proposals.source: passenger car design dimensions
